title: Design a Linked List
statement:
Build your own singly linked list: write a class for its nodes, each with a value and a link to the next node, and a list class that supports these operations, with positions counted from 0.

- `get index` returns the value at position `index`, or `-1` when there is no node there.
- `addAtHead val` adds a node with the value `val` before the first node, so it becomes the new head.
- `addAtTail val` adds a node with the value `val` after the last node.
- `addAtIndex index val` adds a node with the value `val` just before the node at position `index`. When `index` equals the length of the list, the node goes at the end. When `index` is greater than the length, nothing happens.
- `deleteAtIndex index` removes the node at position `index` when there is one, and otherwise does nothing.

The list starts empty. The first line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to each `get` on its own line. Indexes are never negative, and values are whole numbers from 0 to 1000.

Input:

```text
6
addAtHead 1
addAtTail 3
addAtIndex 1 2
get 1
deleteAtIndex 1
get 1
```

Expected output:

```text
2
3
```

hints: Each node holds a value and a link to the next node. The list itself only needs to remember its first node and how many nodes it has.
Inserting or deleting at a position means changing the link of the node just before it. Write one helper that walks to that node.
A dummy node placed before the head means every real node has a node before it, so adding or removing at index 0 needs no special case.
